routes.description: Fine-tuning confirms classical theism over single-universe naturalism because life-permitting parameters are much likelier under a perfectly good designer.
routes.successCriteria: Establish the fine-tuning datum, a favorable likelihood ratio, and a prior-probability advantage over the strongest augmented-naturalist alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Cosmic fine-tuning is strong evidence for classical theism over the relevant naturalistic alternatives.

centralBridges.description: Life-permitting physical parameters are substantially likelier under classical theism than under single-universe naturalism.
Classical theism retains a materially larger intrinsic-prior share than fine-tuning-specific augmented naturalism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Perfect goodness supplies a non-negligible reason for a designer to create embodied moral agents.
Unlimited divine attributes give classical theism coherence unavailable to arbitrary naturalistic specifications.

routes.description: Naturalistic skepticism undercuts the proposed confirmation by broadening the rival space and challenging claims about divine intentions and comparative priors.
routes.successCriteria: Show that relevant naturalistic disjunctions remain live, that divine psychology is insufficiently constrained, or that comparative intrinsic probabilities remain unresolved.

motionBridge.description: Fine-tuning does not supply strong discriminating evidence for God once the live naturalistic alternatives and prior uncertainty are included.

centralBridges.description: Naturalism comprises many specific hypotheses whose combined probability must be compared with the selected theistic hypothesis.
Perfect goodness does not precisely determine what universe or evidence a divine agent would choose.
Coherence, modesty, and parsimony do not yield a securely quantified prior advantage for classical theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Aliens, simulation, and time-travel hypotheses illustrate naturalistic explanations compatible with apparently intentional evidence.
Some apparent fine-tuning may diagnose deficiencies in physical theories rather than a special property requiring design.

sections.title: Fine-tuning likelihood and alternatives
sections.rationale: The opening cases establish the principal likelihood argument and the skeptical expansion of intentional but non-theistic explanations.

sections.title: Hypothesis-space burden

sections.title: Possible evidence and divine psychology
sections.rationale: The resurrection example tests whether contextual evidence can distinguish divine agency from powerful natural agents with uncertain intentions.

sections.title: Comparative intrinsic priors
sections.rationale: The central Bayesian dispute concerns whether perfect-being theism occupies more prior space than fine-tuning-specific naturalistic hypotheses.

sections.title: Coherence, modesty, and parsimony
sections.rationale: The final exchange tests the theoretical-virtue warrant offered for the claimed asymmetry in comparative intrinsic probability.
